name: Binary Search Tree (BST)
description: Binary tree with BST property: left subtree < node < right subtree. Supports O(h) insert, search, and delete where h is tree height.
aim: Maintain a binary tree where left children are smaller and right children are larger, enabling efficient O(log n) average search/insert/delete.
howItWorks: Search: start at root, go left if target < node, right if larger
Insert: follow search path, insert at appropriate null child position
Delete: three cases — leaf (remove directly), one child (bypass), two children (replace with inorder successor)
Height determines performance: O(log n) balanced, O(n) skewed

time.averageCase: Random insertions produce ~O(log n) average height

complexity.spaceDescription: Each node stores value + two child pointers

whenToUse: Frequent search, insert, delete on ordered data
alternatives: AVL Tree or Red-Black Tree — guaranteed O(log n) by balancing
Hash Map — O(1) average but no ordering
Skip List — probabilistic O(log n), simpler to implement
